clue.text: Ultimately deficient stock gets one worker begging

indicators.note: lacking at the end, so the final letter of the word for stock is dropped

parts.note: stock is a supply of goods
one is the Roman numeral I
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A worker in a firm whose stock has run short goes begging.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant person is humbly entreating or pleading, which is what begging describes.

clue.text: Hearts lost to Jesus in, for example, part of church

indicators.note: in places the shortened name inside the word for example

parts.note: say means for example, as in say, a bishop

indicators.note: lost means the hearts letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Jesus is Christ
H is the card players' abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Losing heart to Jesus inside part of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts' looks like courage or devotion, but it is the card suit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is the room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept.

clue.text: "Climbing record broken by English team" — small picture feature

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters reverse
the record is broken open with letters put into its middle

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
XI is eleven, a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A headline about an English team breaking a climbing record, beside a tiny image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' puts EXI inside LP for LEXIP, and 'Climbing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is one of the tiny dots that together make up a digital image.

clue.text: Victims of WW1 the result of power station closure?

definitions.meaning: the young men killed in the First World War, a cohort lost

definitions.text: the result of power station closure?
definitions.meaning: whimsically, when a power station shuts, the power it produced is lost

explanation.surface: Wartime casualties are compared to the fallout when a power plant shuts down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the generation decimated or disillusioned by WW1, and literally means electricity output gone missing.

clue.text: See 14
Destructive force moving mountains? No, no!

indicators.note: moving the letters around shuffles them into a new word

parts.note: these letters are what the shuffle must leave out; the second no! refuses them

explanation.surface: Something so destructive it could move mountains? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, no!' says no to NO: rearranging MOUNTAINS gives the answer plus N and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave capable of enormous destruction, a natural force.

clue.text: Huge online artwork?

parts.note: E is the usual prefix for electronic or online things, as in email
pic is short for picture, a piece of artwork

explanation.surface: An enormous piece of digital art posted on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand in scale, a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Holy Joe restricting foul crone's base benefit

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the prig's letters surround the next word

parts.note: a Holy Joe is a sanctimonious person, a prig
foul means vile

indicators.note: the base of a word in a down clue is its bottom, final letter

explanation.surface: A pious hypocrite confines a foul old woman's foundations, gaining an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: A Holy Joe is a self-righteous person. 'restricting' puts VILE in PRIG; 'base' takes E from 'crone's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or advantage, a synonym for a benefit.

clue.text: Declared source of funding for EU members

indicators.note: declared means said out loud, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: cheques are a means of payment, a source of funds

explanation.surface: An announced source of money for European Union countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of the Czech Republic, a member state of the European Union.

clue.text: Recording to cover item put on by gents after game

definitions.text: item put on by gents after game

parts.note: shooting is filming, recording on camera
a jacket is a cover, as on a book

explanation.surface: Filming a cover for gentlemen after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after game' means hunting game birds, not following a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweed coat with padded shoulders worn by country gentlemen going out to shoot pheasant and grouse.

clue.text: Lightweight directors from company set it back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for it is set down backwards

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, and so for sex

explanation.surface: A firm sets its management back, the directors seeming lightweights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal is an old convention; 'set' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Coxes steer rowing boats and are chosen for their light weight, so they are lightweight directors of a crew.

clue.text: Move family's boundary marker

parts.note: to move someone is to touch them emotionally
a family is a line, a line of descent

explanation.surface: Shifting the line that marks where a family's land ends.
explanation.definitionFit: On a football or rugby pitch the side boundary is marked by this painted line.

clue.text: Bad soldier stops officer in charge retiring — it doesn't make sense

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill feeling

indicators.note: the soldier stops up, plugging the gap inside the officer
retiring means withdrawing, so the officer's letters go backwards

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, the officer in charge
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A bad soldier halting a retreating commander: nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing the noun: illogic is something that doesn't make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogic is reasoning that is unsound, something lacking sense.

clue.text: Axe short tree trunk, one overshadowed by tree

indicators.note: being overshadowed by the tree means sitting under it, so enclosed by its letters

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

indicators.note: short means the final letter of the trunk word is cut off

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Cutting down a stunted trunk that lies in the shade of a bigger tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a tool for felling the tree, but it is the verb meaning scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to scrap it, the same as to abolish it.

clue.text: Commonly a chain letter — I define it differently

definitions.note: the little word a is the everyday example of this part of speech

indicators.note: the clue words are to be arranged differently, an instruction to rearrange their letters

explanation.surface: A chain letter is passed on, the writer saying they'd define it another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the word 'a' itself, which grammarians call by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In English grammar the word a (or an) is the standard example of this determiner.

clue.text: Support train loses time taking 100 aboard

indicators.note: loses means the time letter is dropped
taking means bringing a replacement in
aboard means in the position the dropped letter vacated

parts.note: a train is a retinue, an entourage
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A train is lighter by one carriage of time, but it takes a hundred on.
explanation.walkthrough: A train here is a retinue: the swap of T for C turns ENTOURAGE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage is to back or support someone, giving them heart.

clue.text: Weariest jockeys, in a way

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and jostle, so the letters are moved into position

explanation.surface: Tired riders, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase qualifies a statement as roughly true, so so to speak, just like in a way.

clue.text: Opportunists, possibly, those grasping Persians

definitions.meaning: outsiders who move in to exploit a situation for gain
cryptically, people who bag carpets, Persian being a kind of rug

explanation.surface: Opportunists, perhaps, are those greedy Persians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persians' are rugs, not people; 'possibly' flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The term originally named Northerners who went South after the US Civil War to profit, and now means any exploitative incomer.

clue.text: Constant truncated, presumably

definitions.meaning: cryptically, something truncated has had its end cut off and so is without an end

explanation.surface: Something constant is presumably cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into END and LESS: lacking an end, as a truncated thing does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without stopping is continuous or perpetual, synonyms of constant.

clue.text: This may bore lawman caught up in affray

indicators.note: caught means trapped inside, so the reversed lawman sits within the fight word

parts.note: an affray is a brawl

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the lawman's letters reverse

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American lawman

explanation.surface: A lawman caught up in a fight may well be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is drilling, not tedium. 'up' gives AD, which 'caught' puts in BRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed tool for boring holes in wood.

clue.text: Such words are equivocal, as wife takes stand

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A wife takes a stand while hedging her words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' joins the pieces; EASEL follows W.
explanation.definitionFit: Weasel words are deliberately vague or ambiguous phrasing, used to avoid a clear commitment.

clue.text: Matched question put in to worry journalist

indicators.note: the question letter is put in the middle of the word for worry

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A question inserted to bother a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Things equated have been treated as equal, set against each other as a match.

clue.text: Immovable barrier straddled by a six-footer

indicators.note: to be straddled is to have something sitting astride you, so the barrier goes between the outer letters

parts.note: an ant is an insect, with six feet
a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: An unshiftable barrier with a six-foot-tall figure astride it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall man, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An adamant person is unyielding, refusing to be moved from a position.

clue.text: Wartime show mounted to conceal a fiddle

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the reversed show surrounds the letter
mounted in a down clue means raised upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: ITMA (It's That Man Again) was a hugely popular BBC radio comedy show during WW2

explanation.surface: A wartime show staged to cover up a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: ITMA was a BBC radio comedy of the Second World War. 'mounted' gives AMTI, and 'to conceal' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, and a fiddle is a violin.

clue.text: Broadcast appears over and over again

definitions.text: Broadcast appears over and over again

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
a second O, again an over

explanation.surface: A programme that is aired repeatedly, episode after episode.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a long-running serial drama, while its parts mix APPEARS with two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial drama on TV or radio is aired again and again, several times a week for years.

clue.text: Villain in white van keeps coming round

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the concealed letters read backwards
in shows the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crook lurking in a white van that keeps circling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to EVANK within 'white van keeps', and 'coming round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is an old word for a dishonest rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Welsh representation in Midlands town

definitions.meaning: a national emblem of Wales, the vegetable worn on St David's Day
a market town in Staffordshire, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: Wales sends a representative to a town in central England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is a Welsh national symbol, and it is also the name of a Staffordshire market town.

clue.text: A gem of a game?

definitions.meaning: a single diamond set on its own in a ring
a card or peg game played by one person

explanation.surface: Is this game a real treasure?
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a single precious stone in a setting and a one-player game.
